```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(DT)
library(htmltools)
```

# Load MutSeqR and Example Data

```{r load-lib}
library(MutSeqR)
```

The example data consists of 24 mouse bone marrow DNA samples imported using import_mut_data() and filtered with filter_mut. Data was sequenced on the TS Mouse Mutagenesis Panel. Example data is retrieved from MutSeqRData, an ExperimentHub data package.

```{r load-ex}
library(ExperimentHub)
# load the index
eh <- ExperimentHub()
```

# Bubble Plots

`plot_bubbles` is used to visually represent the distribution and density of
mutations that are observed in multiple reads (multiplets). Each mutation
in a given group is represented by a bubble whose size is scaled on either
the `alt_depth` or the `vaf`. Thus mutations that occur in a large number
of reads are represented by a large bubble. These plots make it easy to
determine if MFmax is driven by a few highly expanded mutations versus
serveral moderately expanded mutations.

Plots can be facetted by user-defined groups, and bubbles can be coloured by
any variable of interest to help discern patterns in mutation recurrence.

_Example 1. Plot mutations per dose group, bubbles coloured by base-6 subtype_

```{r bubbles-cap, include=FALSE}
caption <- paste(
  "Multiplet mutations plotted per Dose. Each circle represents a mutation,",
  "coloured by mutation subtype. The size of the circle is scaled by the",
  "mutation's alternative depth."
)
```

```{r bubble-plot, fig.wide=TRUE, fig.cap=caption}
# load example data:
example_data <- eh[["EH9861"]]

plot <- plot_bubbles(
  mutation_data = example_data,
  size_by = "alt_depth",
  facet_col = "dose_group",
  color_by = "normalized_subtype"
)
plot
```

# Radar Plots

`plot_radar()` is used to visualize mutation frequencies across specified groups as a radar/spider plot.

Data must include a `response_col` (ex. mf_min) and a `label_col` (the variable by which to plot). You may plot multiple groups of data by specifying the group with `group_col`. The radar plots for each group will be overlaid on top of each other in different colours. Colour may be customized with `custom_palette`. Alternatively, you may facet the radar plots by `group_col` by setting `facet = TRUE`. Finally, you may colour the label values by different colours by providing a named vector to `label_colors`.

_Example 2. Plot the mutation frequency for each of the 20 genomic targets of the TwinStrand Mutagenesis Panel. Facet panels by dose group._

```{r radar-cap, include=FALSE}
caption <- paste(
  "Average Minimum Mutation Frequency (mutation/bp) per genomic target.",
  " Plots are facetted by dose group."
)
```

First we will calculate the average MFmin for each genomic target across dose groups. We will also define the order in which the genomic targets should appear on our plot. We will arrange genomic targets ffrom low to high at the High dose group. We will colour our labels based on genic context so that we can visualize differences in mutation frequency driven be genic context. Genic regions will be in black and integernic regions will be labeled in red.

```{r calc-mf}
mf <- calculate_mf(
    mutation_data = example_data,
    cols_to_group = c("sample", "label"),
    retain_metadata_cols = "dose_group"
)
avg <- mf %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dose_group, label) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(mean_mf = mean(mf_min))

label_order <- avg %>%
  dplyr::filter(dose_group == "High") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(mean_mf) %>%
  pull(label)
```

```{r radar-plot, fig.cap=caption, fig.wide=TRUE}
plot <- plot_radar(
    mf_data = avg,
    response_col = "mean_mf",
    label_col = "label",
    group_col = "dose_group",
    facet = FALSE,
    label_order = "custom",
    label_order_input = label_order,
    label_colors = c(
    "chr1" = "#ff0000",
    "chr1.2"	= "#000000",
    "chr2" = "#ff0000",
    "chr3"	= "#000000",
    "chr4"	= "#ff0000",
    "chr5"	= "#ff0000",
    "chr6"	= "#000000",
    "chr7"	= "#000000",
    "chr8"	= "#ff0000",
    "chr9"	= "#000000",
    "chr10"	= "#ff0000",
    "chr11"	= "#ff0000",
    "chr12"	= "#000000",
    "chr13"	= "#000000",
    "chr14"	= "#ff0000",
    "chr15"	= "#000000",
    "chr16"	= "#ff0000",
    "chr17"	= "#ff0000",
    "chr18"	= "#ff0000",
    "chr19"	= "#000000"
  )
)

plot
```

This plot shows us that average mutation frequency increases with dose. Second, intergenic targets (targets on the left of the plot) show higher mutation frequencies compared to genic targets (targets on the right side of the plot).

# Lollipop Plots

`plot_lollipop()`is used to visualize recurrent mutations. Recurrent mutations
may be analysed across the entire data sets or across user-specified
variable(s) (ex. sample, contig, dose). Mutations may also be analysed at the
various subtype resolutions. Mutations i a group that occur above a specified
recurrence threshold are plotted by genomic position. If specified, mutations
are colored by their mutation subtype. For each level in the specified group,
a lollipop plot will be generated and stored in a list.

_Example 3. We will visualize mutations that occur a minimum of 2 times in a group_
_Mutations will be grouped by genomic target (label) and by dose group_
_Recurring mutations will be resolved at the base_6 level_

```{r lolli-cap, include=FALSE}
caption <- paste("Recurrent mutations in target chr 2 found in the High dose group plotted by",
    "genomic position and coloured by normalized subtype. Plots are separated by genomic target.")
```

```{r plot-lollipop, fig.cap=caption, fig.wide=TRUE}
plot_list <- plot_lollipop(
    mutation_data = example_data,
    min_recurrence = 2,
    group_col = c("label", "dose_group"),
    subtype_resolution = "base_6"
)

plot_list[50]

```
